title: Late Breaking Results: Majority-Inverter Graph Minimization by Design Space Exploration
problem: Majority-inverter graphs (MIGs) are used in logic synthesis for emerging technologies, but unlike and-inverter graphs (AIGs), they lack well-developed optimization flows. The paper addresses minimizing MIG size by effectively combining multiple optimization techniques.
motivation: MIGs are critical for logic synthesis in majority-based emerging technologies, and improving their optimization directly impacts the quality of synthesized circuits.
method: The paper uses on-the-fly design space exploration to systematically explore combinations of established MIG optimization algorithms including rewriting, resubstitution, and graph mapping. Different orderings and combinations of these techniques are evaluated to discover superior optimization flows.
key_novelty: On-the-fly design space exploration to systematically combine existing MIG optimization algorithms, achieving better results than fixed optimization flows.
contributions: Design space exploration methodology for combining MIG optimization algorithms
State-of-the-art MIG minimization results on EPFL benchmarks with 14% average improvement over prior flows
Demonstration of up to 88% and 79% size reductions on specific benchmark cases

metrics.area: 14% average improvement, maximum 88% reduction on specific benchmarks

primary_theme: Circuit synthesis optimization via design space exploration
